items.title: Somalia: Xawaadle Elders and Al-Shabaab Reportedly Reach Truce in Hiiraan
items.description: A 16-point joint statement circulated by Al-Shabaab-affiliated media  said the sides had resolved their disputes and agreed to maintain peace in areas controlled or influenced by the clan. The reported agreement includes a commitment by Hawadle elders not to allow the recruitment or operation of Macawiisley fighters in their areas or provide them with shelter. Macawiisley forces from Hiiraan have played a key role in supporting Somali government troops against Al-Shabaab. The meeting in Maxaas was attended by dozens of traditional elders, while Al-Shabaab was represented by senior figures

items.description: It was the latest wave in a displacement crisis that has been building in Somalia's Lower Shabelle region for a decade, and there is no sign it is reversing. items.title: African leaders call for continent to unlock capital at Egypt business summit
items.description: African heads of state and business leaders gathered in Egypt on Saturday for the inaugural El-Alamein Africa Forum. They called for the continent to unlock its capital to finance growth and reduce reliance on external funding.
items.titleIt: African leaders call for continent to unlock capital at Egypt business summit

items.title: Sudan: WFP Strongly Condemns Attack On Trucks In South Kordofan, Killing One Driver
items.description: One driver was killed in the air strike. We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends and colleagues. The contracted trucks were en route from Dilling to Kadugli and clearly marked as humanitarian vehicles. Additional details regarding the circumstances of the incident, including the extent of the damage to the food cargo, are still being collected. WFP calls for a prompt and impartial investigation into this incident and for those responsible for any violations to be held accountable. items.title: AU, U.S. Call for De-escalation as Tensions Rise in Tigray
items.description: African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf expressed concern over reports that Tigray forces had seized the airports in Mekelle, Axum and Shire, detained federal personnel and disrupted civilian air services. Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights to the three destinations on Wednesday, citing the "current situation" in the region, according to Addis Standard. The airline said passengers would be notified when services resume.
